messages.subject: plot options
parts:
Hello everyone;

I have two sets of responses (5-point scale) to the same question -- one from teachers and the other from principals. Teachers and Principals are grouped in buildings. What I want to do is be able to generate, for each Principal, a plot that shows their response to each question and the average Teacher response.

I suppose I could do this via bars but would ideally like to use points such that when the Principal response equals the Teacher response the result is a single point of a specific color. When the responses differ across the Principal and the Teacher(s)' average the points are spaced apart. Sample data will be as follows (Principal/Teacher = 1 if Principal; 2 if Teacher):

Building Principal/Teacher Question1 Question2
1 1 5 5
1 2 2 1
1 2 3 1
1 2 5 1
2 1 4 4
2 2 4 3
: : : :

What would be the cleanest way to do this via ggplot2? Any tips would be greatly appreciated. I will continue to monkey with ggplot2 while I see if anyone has some brilliant ideas.

thanks!

Ani

Hi:

I've got an idea as follows:

df <- read.csv("Book1.csv", header=T) # data file attached in this email

#MELT DATA
require(reshape)
md <- melt(df, id=(c("Building", "Principal.Teacher")))

#DRAW THE PLOT (attached to this email)
require(ggplot2)
ggplot(md, aes(factor(Building), value)) +
geom_point(aes(shape=factor(Principal.Teacher), colour=factor(Principal.Teacher)))

Not sure that's what you'd like.

Cheers Trong.
